executive_assessment.text: Gwembe/Sinazongwe drought recovery and Lundazi/Lumezi flood-water disruption illustrate different local livelihoods and service vulnerabilities.
Cash and borehole outputs are reported activities; recipient perceptions identify inclusion/access concerns but do not establish causal effects or representative district comparisons.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-05-08 reports: The 2023/2024 season’s late onset, dry spells and heat affected crops and livestock; over nine million people in 84 of 117 districts were affected, with Central, Eastern, Southern and Western provinces hardest hit.
Source dated 2025-09 reports: Among 950 surveyed assistance recipients, 66.7% said aid met household priorities; 27.3% disagreed, citing unmet needs, exclusion or access barriers.
The recipient survey reports different protection-service perceptions in Lunga and Gwembe and identifies remoteness, roads and communications as constraints.

Source dated 2026-03-20 reports: FAO reports that drought-damaged crops, dried water sources and livestock losses persisted in Gwembe and Sinazongwe after above-average 2025/2026 rains supported crop recovery; some households entered later seasons with depleted herds and assets.

Source dated 2026-03-20 reports: FAO and partners distributed 1,312 goats to vulnerable farmers in Gwembe and Sinazongwe, reporting about 1,600 people reached, a majority women; support also included animal husbandry, disease-control and climate-smart agriculture training.

Source dated 2026-03-20 reports: A woman farmer from Luumbo Camp, Munyumbwe, told FAO she had lost livestock in the drought and received replacement goats; the project says a pass-on arrangement is intended to extend offspring to other households.

Source dated 2026-01-30 reports: Late-December 2025 floods in Lundazi and Lumezi submerged Lundazi’s treatment plant, leaving over 40,000 people without safe water; UNICEF describes child displacement, missed school, crop losses and greater illness risk.

Source dated 2026-01-30 reports: UNICEF reported orienting over 75 community volunteers across four flood-affected health facilities and 11 additional facilities remotely; three hand pumps were provided for installation and three clinic boreholes remained planned.
